content.overview: Section 10 permits parties to determine the number of arbitrators, but the number shall not be even; where an even number has been agreed, section 10(2) supplies the statutory consequence.
content.glance: Section 10 permits parties to determine the number of arbitrators, but the number shall not be even; where an even number has been agreed, section 10(2) supplies the statutory consequence.
content.study:
Module 1: Composition
The tribunal's numerical composition is governed first by party agreement, subject to the statutory prohibition on an even number.

Module 2: Even-number agreement
Where parties agree on an even number, section 10(2) supplies the statutory consequence; the provision must not be confused with the appointment procedure in section 11.

Module 3: Application
Identify the arbitration agreement, determine the agreed number and then apply the statutory composition rule.

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: A clause provides for three arbitrators; the composition is consistent with section 10.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: A clause provides for two arbitrators; section 10(2) must be applied rather than treating the two-member arrangement as conclusively operative.

misconceptions.correction: Apply section 10 with its express conditions and neighbouring provisions.
